title: Semantics is non-independent: class S is defined by quoting the NL axioms/rules (circular, trivial soundness/completeness)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Definition `def:matrix`, condition (M3); Theorem `thm:sound`; Proposition `prop:LTmatrix`.

**Gap.** An `NL`-matrix is *defined* (M3) by the requirement that *every instance of every NL axiom scheme is designated*, and (M1)/(M2) directly encode MP/Adj. Hence the class
$$S=\{\mathfrak M:\mathfrak M\text{ validates all NL axioms and is closed under MP, Adj}\}.$$
With this definition:
- **Soundness** (Thm `thm:sound`) is true by *unwinding the definition*; no property of any connective ($\neg,\wedge,\vee,\to$) is ever used. In particular the connexive content (that B1,B2,A9,A10 are simultaneously satisfiable in a non-degenerate structure) is *assumed as a membership clause*, not proved.
- **Completeness** is then near-tautological: the Lindenbaum–Tarski matrix lies in $S$ precisely because $S$ was defined to contain *every* matrix validating the axioms.

This construction works **verbatim for any Hilbert calculus**, including inconsistent ones, and conveys no information about NL specifically.

**Why this is a genuine gap.** The problem asks to *construct a formal semantics* (relational, algebraic, or many-valued) and *exhibit a class of structures*. A class whose defining clause is literally ``designates all NL-axioms and is closed under NL-rules'' is the canonical non-answer: it gives no *intrinsic* (equational / quasi-equational / frame-condition) characterization of the operations. Faithfulness (F1) failure.

**What is required.** Replace (M3) by *intrinsic* algebraic/relational conditions and then *prove* each axiom (esp. the connexive B1/B2 and contraposition A9) is valid from those conditions. E.g. define an NL-algebra as a bounded distributive lattice $(A,\wedge,\vee)$ with a designated filter $D$, an involutive order-reversing negation ($\neg\neg a=a$, A10; $a\le b\Rightarrow\neg b\le\neg a$, A9), a transitive relevant implication with $a\le b\iff a\to b\in D$ (A1,A2,A4–A7), plus the connexive (in)equalities $a\to b\le\neg(a\to\neg b)$ and $a\to\neg b\le\neg(a\to b)$ (B1,B2); OR a Routley–Meyer frame $(W,R,\ast,\le)$ with a frame condition forcing the connexive theses. Then prove soundness by checking the axioms and completeness via Lindenbaum–Tarski showing the quotient satisfies the *intrinsic* conditions.
